questions.prompt: What distinguishes a sample from a population in inferential statistics?

options.text: Sample size is larger than population size
Population is a subset of the sample
Sample is a subset of the population
Population is derived from the sample

questions.explanation: A sample is a subset drawn from the larger population; it is not larger than the population.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the Central Limit Theorem?

options.text: The distribution of sample means becomes normal as sample size increases
The distribution of population means becomes normal as sample size increases
Sample mean always equals population mean
The distribution of sample variances is normal for small samples

questions.explanation: As sample size grows, the sampling distribution of the mean approaches normality regardless of the population shape.

questions.prompt: In a hypothesis test, a p‑value of 0.03 indicates:

options.text: There is a 3% chance the null hypothesis is true
The observed data would be unlikely if the null hypothesis were true
We should reject the null hypothesis at alpha=0.05
Both b and c

questions.explanation: A p‑value of 0.03 means the data are unlikely under the null, so we reject at alpha 0.05.

questions.prompt: A 95% confidence interval for a mean is (10, 14). Which statement is correct?

options.text: We are 95% confident that the true mean lies between 10 and 14
There is a 95% chance that the true mean is between 10 and 14
95% of sample means will fall between 10 and 14
The interval has a 5% chance of containing the true mean

questions.explanation: The interval captures the true mean 95% of the time across repeated samples.

questions.prompt: Two studies both find a statistically significant difference with p<0.05, but one has a very small effect size. Which statement is most accurate?

options.text: The study with the smaller effect size is more important
Statistical significance always implies practical significance
The study with the smaller effect size may not be practically meaningful
Effect size is irrelevant if p<0.05

questions.explanation: A small effect size means the difference, while statistically significant, may lack practical importance.

questions.prompt: In a power analysis for a two‑sample t‑test, increasing the sample size from 30 to 60 per group while holding alpha constant will:

options.text: Decrease power
Increase power
Keep power unchanged
Increase alpha

questions.explanation: More subjects increase the ability to detect a true effect, thereby raising power.
